assumptions.statement: Recreating a table preserves the row-level security policies that applied to the original table.
The grants restored by the migration are sufficient to preserve the tenant boundary.

facts.evidence_ref: cases/C01/candidate.sql: DROP TABLE payments; ALTER TABLE payments_new RENAME TO payments
facts.statement: The migration drops and recreates the payments table rather than using ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN.

facts.evidence_ref: cases/C01/candidate.sql: GRANT statements after the rename
facts.statement: The migration restores SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE grants for aidledger_app and aidledger_service, and SELECT for aidledger_org_admin.

facts.evidence_ref: cases/C01/candidate.sql: full text, searched for POLICY and ROW LEVEL SECURITY
facts.statement: The migration contains no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, no FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and no CREATE POLICY statement.
The policy declares four tenant-scoped roles and twelve access probes over payments and audit_events.
The visible test checks column presence, row count and the foreign key, and does not query as a tenant-scoped role.

invariants.description: No session may read rows belonging to an organisation other than its own.
invariants.executable_check: Connect as each tenant-scoped role with a session organisation set, query payments filtered to a different organisation, and require zero rows.

invariants.description: Every declared role retains the access the policy grants it.
invariants.executable_check: Connect as each declared role and confirm its own-tenant reads and writes still succeed with the expected row counts.

invariants.description: No declared role gains access the policy does not grant it.
invariants.executable_check: Attempt each operation the policy denies and require SQLSTATE 42501.

summary: The candidate adds settlement_reference to payments by rewriting the table: create payments_new, copy, drop the original, rename, then restore grants. Grants are restored explicitly; nothing in the migration restores row-level security, which was an attribute of the dropped table.

unknowns.question: Whether the deployment process applies policies separately from migrations.
